desc:
The following process is applied to the integer array nums. In each round, every element that is strictly smaller than the element immediately to its left (in the current array) is marked, and then all marked elements are removed at the same time. The process stops when no element is removed, i.e. when the array is non-decreasing.

Return the number of rounds in which at least one element is removed.

Example: nums = [5, 3, 4, 4, 7, 3, 6, 11, 8, 5, 11] gives 3. Round 1 removes 3, 3, 8 and 5 and leaves [5, 4, 4, 7, 6, 11, 11]; round 2 removes 4 and 6 and leaves [5, 4, 7, 11, 11]... wait, only elements smaller than their left neighbor go, so round 2 leaves [5, 7, 11, 11] after removing the 4 (smaller than 5) and the 6 (smaller than 7); round 3 has nothing left to remove, so the answer would be 2 here.
hints: Simulating rounds directly can take up to n rounds of O(n) work each. Ask instead: in which round does each individual element disappear?
Element x is removed in the round after everything between it and its 'blocker' (the nearest element to its left that is strictly greater) has been removed, but only if such a blocker exists.

Use a stack of (value, round of removal) pairs from left to right. For a new element, pop all elements with value ≤ x and take the maximum of their removal rounds t. If the stack is then empty, x is never removed (round 0); otherwise its round is t + 1. The answer is the largest round.
editorial: Let dp[i] be the round in which element i is removed (0 if it never is). Element i is only ever removed if some element to its left is strictly greater: let p be the nearest such element. Everything strictly between p and i is ≤ nums[i]. The element i becomes adjacent to p once all of those in-between elements are gone, which happens after max(dp[k]) rounds over them; in the next round it is exposed to p and removed. So dp[i] = 1 + max(dp[k] for k between p and i), or 0 when no such p exists.

A monotonic stack computes this in one pass. Keep (value, dp) pairs with strictly decreasing values from bottom to top. For element x, pop all pairs with value ≤ x and take the maximum of their dp values, t (0 if none popped). If the stack is empty after the pops, dp = 0; otherwise dp = t + 1. Push (x, dp) and update the global maximum, which is the answer. O(n) time, O(n) space.
solution:
def roundsToSorted(nums):
    best = 0
    stack = []  # (value, round in which it is removed); values strictly decreasing
    for x in nums:
        t = 0
        while stack and stack[-1][0] <= x:
            t = max(t, stack.pop()[1])
        t = t + 1 if stack else 0
        best = max(best, t)
        stack.append((x, t))
    return best
